messages.subject: sparse matrices & AR 1 processes
parts:
We've been having a discussion with a third party I
thought I'd bring onto the list.

The >> are from me and >>> and > are from Ben.

>> There's no obstacle in principle to adding sparse matrices, other than that Eigen probably doesn't support the
>> same set of operations on them, and we'd have to add a whole new set of expression templates to deal vectorizing
>> them.
>
> Right. Although with 3.1.x, they brought sparse almost up to par with dense.

That's really good news.

>>> As I've said to Bob and Andrew in the past, about the only thing that is good about the Wishart-family priors is
>>> that they are conjugate with something, which is irrelevant unless you are doing Gibbs sampling, which Stan is
>>> not doing. The biggest advantage of Stan's LKJ priors is that you can put a joint uniform prior on the
>>> correlation matrix and whatever prior you want on the standard deviations, plus it is easy to shrink the
>>> correlation prior toward the identity matrix. Other problems may have AR1 structure or something else, which Stan
>>> could easily handle but does not at the moment.
>>
>> I'm probably missing something about Stan not handling AR1 structure.
>
> Stan can do it, particularly if the user can hack the .stan file, but we don't have any awesome C++ to handle the
> covariance or correlation matrix of an AR1 process. If rho is the auto-regressive parameter, the entries of the
> correlation matrix are powers of rho. And the precision matrix is tridiagonal and known analytically. So, it would be
> inefficient to plow that through multivariate_normal_log().

Ah -- that's what I was missing.

I'll add it to the to-do list :-)

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] sparse matrices & AR 1 processes
parts:
Ben
Can you please remind me of what the lkj prior is.  Are there references on it?  I'm wondering because maybe I should include this in BDA.
A

As I've said to Bob and Andrew in the past, about the only thing  that is good about the Wishart-family priors is
that they are conjugate with something, which is irrelevant unless you  are doing Gibbs sampling, which Stan is
not doing. The biggest advantage of Stan's LKJ priors is that you can put a joint  uniform prior on the
correlation matrix and whatever prior you want on the standard deviations, plus it is easy to  shrink the
correlation prior toward the identity matrix. Other problems may have AR1 structure or something else, which Stan
could easily handle but does not at the moment.
